items.findings: Quotes verbatim at the locators (title p. 1, introduction p. 1, conclusion p. 9); 'up to 2 trillion tokens' is in the abstract; publication June 2007 from the proceedings footer is right. Sense: n-gram models distinguished by scale, which meets the criterion as worded. Earliest-located role refuted by an independent search: Hu, Turin and Brown, 'Language modeling with stochastic automata', Proc. ICSLP 96 (Philadelphia, 3-6 October 1996), pp. 406-409, doi:10.21437/ICSLP.1996-79, abstract: 'large language models are often required to achieve low model perplexity (or entropy) and still have adequate language coverage'. That is a statistical language model distinguished by model size, which meets the criterion as currently worded (the paper's body contrasts entropy against 'model size'). Found through the Semantic Scholar bulk search (abstract), confirmed in the ISCA Archive PDF (cached as b-audit-hu-1996, PDF p. 1). The pack's search covered the ACL Anthology, Crossref titles and arXiv, not the ISCA Archive (ICSLP/Eurospeech/Interspeech).
items.proposedFix: Apply the corrections rule: make Hu, Turin and Brown (ICSLP 96, October 1996, ISCA Archive PDF) the earliest-located-term record for th-term-large-language-model, quoting the abstract sentence; change Brants et al. 2007 to role 'use' and keep its displaced headline as a correction dated 2026-10-29 with the reason. Add the ISCA Archive and Semantic Scholar abstracts to the 'How we searched' note, and record that speech venues are now partly covered. Alternatively, if the maintainer wants a narrower criterion (e.g. a name for a class of models rather than an adjective-plus-noun phrase), say so in the criterion; under such a criterion Brants 2007 would need the same re-test, since its uses ('very large language models') are also adjectival.

items.findings: Quote verbatim (PDF p. 1, abstract); arXiv v1 2021-08-16 confirmed by the arXiv API. Sense meets the criterion. The quoted sentence 'We call these models foundation models...' does not on its own carry the statement's description; the referent is in the preceding abstract sentence. Quick independent search (arXiv API abstract phrase search; Semantic Scholar bulk search 'foundation models' with ML terms, 2010-2021) found only engineering senses and the later-revised arXiv items the pack already discounts (2010.03688, 2101.09858, 1810.13306); no earlier ML-sense use.
items.proposedFix: Add to the evidence the preceding abstract sentence: 'models (e.g., BERT, DALL-E, GPT-3) that are trained on broad data at scale and are adaptable to a wide range of downstream tasks' (PDF p. 1, abstract), so the statement's description is quoted, not inferred from 'these models'.

items.findings: Both quotes verbatim (p. 1 abstract; p. 10 conclusion); v1 2017-06-12 confirmed. items.proposedFix: Optional: name the arXiv title check (and Spatial Transformer Networks as a known other sense) in the family's 'How we searched' note.

items.findings: The quotation is not continuous: the ellipsis replaces 'and I did sort of commission its creation!' (second paragraph of the post). The omitted words are Goertzel's own partial self-credit and bear directly on the record's subject (Goertzel crediting himself), so the cut changes what the passage says about his role. Also, the passage is the second paragraph, not 'second and third sentences of the post' (the first paragraph is one sentence; the second has three). Date 2011-08-28 confirmed on the page.
items.proposedFix: Statement: 'In his 2011 post Goertzel says he is responsible for spreading the term AGI around the world and "did sort of commission its creation", but did not coin the phrase.' Quote the passage without the gap, or use two quotes: 'I am indeed the one responsible for spreading the term around the world' and 'and I did sort of commission its creation! But I didn't actually coin the phrase'. Locator: 'second paragraph'. Contribution: add 'commissioning its creation (by his account)'.

items.findings: Quote verbatim in the page as served on 2026-10-29. The record's date (2014, claimed) misdates the wording: the same opening paragraph says 'In 2020, we celebrated BP's half-century anniversary!' and 'In the 2020s, it was still easy to find misleading accounts', so the quoted text is at least 2020 wording and probably 2025. The 2014 survey (arXiv v4, b-schmidhuber-2014 p. 11) says 'apparently was first described in a 1970 master's thesis', a different, hedged wording. Under the policy's two-dates rule the attested date of this wording is the retrieval state (page last updated 2025 by its own statement), not 2014. Shown alone, a 2014 date would mislead a reader into placing this statement before the 2015 Nature review.
items.proposedFix: Set the time to the attested wording: date 2025 (page's latest stated update) or 2026-10-29 (retrieval), basis 'attested in the page as served 2026-10-29', with 2014 shown only as the page's claimed first version. Optionally add a separate attributed record from the 2014 survey's own hedged sentence ('apparently was first described in a 1970 master's thesis (Linnainmaa, 1970, 1976)', p. 11) if a 2014-dated statement is wanted.

items.findings: Quote verbatim in the page as served. Same dating problem as the Linnainmaa record, and here demonstrably so: the 2014 survey (arXiv v4, p. 11) says the first NN-specific application 'was described in 1981 (Werbos, 1981, 2006)' and cites 'some preliminary, NN-specific discussion (Werbos, 1974, section 5.5.1)', whereas the page says 1982 and 'not yet in his 1974 thesis'. So the quoted wording did not exist in 2014; dating it 2014 (claimed) is wrong. The side-by-side disagreement with LeCun, Bengio and Hinton 2015 is correctly recorded, but the chronology of the disagreement is inverted by the misdate.
items.proposedFix: Date the record by the attested wording (2025 update / served 2026-10-29), keep 2014 only as the page's claimed origin, and add to the qualification that the author's 2014 survey gave 1981 and a 'preliminary, NN-specific discussion' in Werbos 1974 (b-schmidhuber-2014, PDF p. 11), so the author's own account changed between versions.
